plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 after compilation failure due to layer count mismatch (declared 20, actual 21). Three new routes fix this by explicitly stating exact layer counts in both topology and execution request. Route 1 uses Ge/YbF3 with exactly 22 layers in a dual-cavity defect design. Route 2 uses ZnS/MgF2 with exactly 20 layers in a combined long-pass/short-pass topology. Route 3 uses Ge/SiO2 with exactly 24 layers maximizing the layer budget for steeper edges. All routes preserve the dual-band pass requirement (3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm) and dual stopband suppression (2.50-3.10 μm and 4.45-5.00 μm) on CaF2 substrate.

routes.title: Ge/YbF3 Dual-Cavity Defect Filter with Exact 22-Layer Count
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A dual-cavity defect structure using high-index Ge and low-index YbF3 can simultaneously transmit two narrow bands (3.25-3.35 μm and 4.20-4.30 μm) while blocking adjacent regions, with cavity positions and thicknesses optimized under TMM.
routes.design_principle: Two resonant cavities separated by distributed Bragg reflector sections, each cavity tuned to one passband center wavelength via defect layer thickness. Quarter-wave stack mirrors provide out-of-band blocking.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/YbF3]_4 | Ge_defect1 | [YbF3/Ge]_3 | YbF3_defect2 | [Ge/YbF3]_4 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 22 (8 mirror pairs + 2 defect layers).
design_variables: Defect layer positions fixed at layers 9 and 16
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 22, within 24-layer limit
Ge and YbF3 are conventional IR dielectrics with established deposition processes
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg mirrors
Defect cavity resonance theory for narrow passbands
expected_advantages: High index contrast (Ge ~4.0, YbF3 ~1.5) enables strong blocking with fewer layers
Dual-cavity design naturally supports two independent passbands
known_risks: Ge has absorption in mid-IR that may reduce peak transmittance
Cavity coupling may cause passband interaction if spacing is incorrect
Previous route_03 failed due to layer count mismatch - this route explicitly declares 22 layers
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer stack on CaF2 substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: Layer1=Ge, Layer2=YbF3, Layer3=Ge, Layer4=YbF3, Layer5=Ge, Layer6=YbF3, Layer7=Ge, Layer8=YbF3, Layer9=Ge(defect1), Layer10=YbF3, Layer11=Ge, Layer12=YbF3, Layer13=Ge, Layer14=YbF3, Layer15=Ge, Layer16=YbF3(defect2), Layer17=Ge, Layer18=YbF3, Layer19=Ge, Layer20=YbF3, Layer21=Ge, Layer22=YbF3. All thicknesses bounded [300, 1500] nm. Optimize for: maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm, maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm, minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm. Use TMM solver with normal incidence, unpolarized light. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 2500-3100 nm, 3250-3350 nm, 4200-4300 nm, 4450-5000 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 3.25-3.35 um and 4.20-4.30 um bands; Low transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: High transmittance in 2.50-3.10 um and 4.45-5.00 um bands. manufacturing constraints: Total layer count <= 24; No metal layers; Conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Previous route_03 failed compilation due to layer count mismatch (declared 20, actual 21). This route explicitly declares exactly 22 layers in both topology description and execution request to prevent mismatch. Material pair Ge/YbF3 retained from prior attempt but with corrected layer count and expanded thickness bounds [300, 1500] nm to ensure geometric feasibility.

routes.title: ZnS/MgF2 Combined Long-Pass/Short-Pass Filter with Exact 20-Layer Count
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A combined long-pass and short-pass filter structure using ZnS (medium-high index) and MgF2 (low index) can create two transmission windows by stacking a long-pass section (transmits >3.2 μm) followed by a short-pass section (transmits <4.3 μm).
routes.design_principle: Long-pass section uses increasing layer thicknesses toward substrate to transmit longer wavelengths. Short-pass section uses decreasing thicknesses toward air to transmit shorter wavelengths. Combined effect creates bandpass behavior.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [MgF2/ZnS]_5 (short-pass section) | [ZnS/MgF2]_5 (long-pass section) | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 20 (10 pairs).
design_variables: Layer sequence fixed as alternating pairs
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 20, within 24-layer limit
ZnS and MgF2 are well-established IR coating materials
Lower index contrast than Ge/YbF3 but lower absorption
theory_basis: Long-pass/short-pass combination theory for bandpass filters
expected_advantages: Lower material absorption than Ge-based designs
Well-characterized deposition processes for ZnS and MgF2
20 layers provides margin for manufacturing tolerance
known_risks: Lower index contrast may require more layers for equivalent blocking
Two separate passbands may be harder to achieve with simple long-pass/short-pass combination
May not achieve narrow bandwidth required for gas sensing

routes.title: Ge/SiO2 Maximum-Layer Dual-Band Filter with Exact 24-Layer Count
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Using the maximum allowed 24 layers with high index contrast Ge/SiO2 pair enables steeper spectral edges and deeper blocking than lower-layer-count designs, potentially achieving both narrow passbands simultaneously.
routes.design_principle: Three-cavity design with two passband cavities and one coupling cavity between them. Maximum layer count allows thicker mirror stacks for improved out-of-band blocking while maintaining passband transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/SiO2]_5 | Ge_cavity1 | [SiO2/Ge]_4 | SiO2_cavity2 | [Ge/SiO2]_4 | Ge_cavity3 | [SiO2/Ge]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total finite layers: 24 (12 pairs + 3 cavity layers counted in pairs).
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count exactly 24, at maximum allowed limit
Ge/SiO2 pair has very high index contrast for strong blocking
24 layers may challenge deposition uniformity but is within stated constraint
theory_basis: Multi-cavity filter theory for multiple passbands
Index contrast determines blocking strength per layer pair
expected_advantages: Maximum layer count enables deepest blocking in stopbands
High Ge/SiO2 index contrast provides strong reflection per pair
Three-cavity design offers more degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
known_risks: 24 layers at limit may have manufacturing challenges
SiO2 may have absorption in mid-IR range
Complex cavity coupling may cause passband distortion
Previous route_03 layer count error must be avoided

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:227248144 supports quarter-wave stack design principle used in all three routes, noting that more layers produce steeper slopes and higher blocking.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:136080761 supports long-pass/short-pass combination approach in route_03_refine_02 for bandpass filter construction.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:139773493 supports gas sensor bandpass optimization principle, emphasizing center wavelength and bandwidth as critical parameters.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:17683472 supports thickness-constrained design principle, noting infrared coatings limited to ~40 micrometers total thickness.
Prior route_03 compilation failure (layer count mismatch) directly influenced all three routes to explicitly declare exact layer counts in both topology and execution request.
unresolved_decisions: Optimal material pair for mid-IR dual-band filter remains uncertain - Ge/YbF3, ZnS/MgF2, and Ge/SiO2 all have trade-offs between index contrast and absorption.
Whether two-cavity or three-cavity topology better achieves dual-band separation with narrow bandwidths requires experimental comparison.
Incidence angle not specified in original request - all routes assume normal incidence but satellite payload may require off-angle performance.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
